cases.sentence: Пьер был в Петербурге, куда он поехал по своим ___, как он говорил, на три недели, и где он теперь проживал уже седьмую.
cases.explain: «особенным делам» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was the eve of St. Nikoláy, the fifth of December, 1820. Natásha had been staying at her brother’s with her husband and children since early autumn. Pierre had gone to Petersburg on business of his own for three weeks as he said, but had remained there nearly seven weeks and was expected back every minute.

cases.sentence: 5-го декабря, кроме семейства Безуховых, у Ростовых гостил еще ___ Николая, отставной генерал Василий Федорович Денисов.
cases.explain: «старый друг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Besides the Bezúkhov family, Nikoláy’s old friend the retired General Vasíli Fëdorovich Denísov was staying with the Rostóvs this fifth of December.

cases.sentence: До обеда Николай поверил счеты бурмистра из ___, по именью племянника жены, написал два письма по делам и прошелся на гумно, скотный и конный дворы.
cases.explain: «Рязанской деревни» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On the sixth, which was his name day when the house would be full of visitors, Nikoláy knew he would have to exchange his Tartar tunic for a tail coat, and put on narrow boots with pointed toes, and drive to the new church he had built, and then receive visitors who would come to congratulate him, offer them refreshments, and talk about the elections of the nobility; but he considered himself entitled to spend the eve of that day in his usual way. He examined the bailiff’s accounts of the village in Ryazán which belonged to his wife’s nephew, wrote two business letters, and walked over to the granaries, cattle yards and stables before dinner. Having taken precautions against the general drunkenness to be expected on the morrow because it was a great saint’s day, he returned to dinner, and without having time for a private talk with his wife sat down at the long table laid for twenty persons, at which the whole household had assembled. At that table were his mother, his mother’s old lady companion Belóva, his wife, their three children with their governess and tutor, his wife’s nephew with his tutor, Sónya, Denísov, Natásha, her three children, their governess, and old Mikháil Ivánovich, the late prince’s architect, who was living on in retirement at Bald Hills.

cases.explain: «противоположном конце» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Countess Márya sat at the other end of the table. When her husband took his place she concluded, from the rapid manner in which after taking up his table napkin he pushed back the tumbler and wineglass standing before him, that he was out of humor, as was sometimes the case when he came in to dinner straight from the farm—especially before the soup. Countess Márya well knew that mood of his, and when she herself was in a good frame of mind quietly waited till he had had his soup and then began to talk to him and make him admit that there was no cause for his ill-humor. But today she quite forgot that and was hurt that he should be angry with her without any reason, and she felt unhappy. She asked him where he had been. He replied. She again inquired whether everything was going well on the farm. Her unnatural tone made him wince unpleasantly and he replied hastily.

cases.sentence: Он неприятно поморщился от ее ___ и поспешно ответил.

cases.sentence: Николай жил с своею женой так хорошо, что даже Соня и ___, желавшие, из ревности, несогласия между ними,не могли найти предлога для упрека; но и между ними бывали минуты враждебности.
cases.explain: «старая графиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Nikoláy and his wife lived together so happily that even Sónya and the old countess, who felt jealous and would have liked them to disagree, could find nothing to reproach them with; but even they had their moments of antagonism. Occasionally, and it was always just after they had been happiest together, they suddenly had a feeling of estrangement and hostility, which occurred most frequently during Countess Márya’s pregnancies, and this was such a time.

cases.sentence: Иногда, именно после самых ___, на них находило вдруг чувство отчужденности и враждебности; это чувство являлось чаще всего во времена беременности графини Марьи.
cases.explain: «счастливых периодов» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Она посмотрела на свой высокий живот и в зеркало на свое желто-бледное и исхудавшее лицо с более, чем когда-нибудь, ___.
cases.explain: «большими глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “That’s always the way,” thought Countess Márya. “He talks to everyone except me. I see … I see that I am repulsive to him, especially when I am in this condition.” She looked down at her expanded figure and in the glass at her pale, sallow, emaciated face in which her eyes now looked larger than ever.

cases.sentence: Соня всегда была ___, который избирала графиня Марья для своего раздражения.
cases.explain: «первым предлогом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sónya was always the first excuse Countess Márya found for feeling irritated.

cases.sentence: Она села, поиграла с ними, но мысль о муже и о ___ его, не переставая, мучила ее.
cases.explain: «беспричинной досаде» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The children were playing at “going to Moscow” in a carriage made of chairs and invited her to go with them. She sat down and played with them a little, but the thought of her husband and his unreasonable crossness worried her. She got up and, walking on tiptoe with difficulty, went to the small sitting room.

cases.sentence: — Андрюша, ___, подражая ей, пошел за ней на цыпочках.
cases.explain: «старший мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Perhaps he is not asleep; I’ll have an explanation with him,” she said to herself. Andrúsha, her eldest boy, imitating his mother, followed her on tiptoe. She did not notice him.

cases.sentence: Черноглазая девочка смело скрыпнула дверью, подошла энергическими шажками ___ к дивану и, рассмотрев положение отца, спавшего к ней спиною, поднялась на цыпочках и поцеловала лежавшую под головой руку отца.
cases.explain: «тупых ножек» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Nikoláy coughed and said no more. Countess Márya moved away from the door and took the boy back to the nursery. Five minutes later little black-eyed three-year-old Natásha, her father’s pet, having learned from her brother that Papa was asleep and Mamma was in the sitting room, ran to her father unobserved by her mother. The dark-eyed little girl boldly opened the creaking door, went up to the sofa with energetic steps of her sturdy little legs, and having examined the position of her father, who was asleep with his back to her, rose on tiptoe and kissed the hand which lay under his head. Nikoláy turned with a tender smile on his face.

cases.sentence: — «Опять», с ___ сказала она, указывая на то место, куда Николай поцеловал жену.
cases.explain: «повелительным жестом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Again!” she commanded, pointing with a peremptory gesture to the spot where Nikoláy had placed the kiss.

cases.sentence: — Лицо ее просияло улыбкой; но в то же самое время она вздохнула, и тихая грусть выразилась в ее ___.
cases.explain: «глубоком взгляде» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Countess Márya remained in the sitting room. “I should never, never have believed that one could be so happy,” she whispered to herself. A smile lit up her face but at the same time she sighed, and her deep eyes expressed a quiet sadness as though she felt, through her happiness, that there is another sort of happiness unattainable in this life and of which she involuntarily thought at that instant.
